headline: The biggest adjustment is that everyday warmth — cheek kisses, the OK sign, left-handed eating, feet up — reads very differently in the UAE, so switch to right-hand, verbal, and modest defaults.

watch_outs.title: Left hand at the table
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, eating with a fork and spoon in either hand is completely normal and won't be noticed.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, the left hand is considered unclean; eat, pass dishes, and accept food with your right hand.
watch_outs.do: Use your right hand for all food, drinks, and passing plates, even if you are left-handed.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not reach for a shared platter or hand a dish to your host with your left hand.

watch_outs.title: Cheek-kiss greetings
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, a light cheek-to-cheek greeting with a soft 'mwah' is common among friends and family.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, mirror a same-gender cheek greeting only if the other person leads; with the opposite gender, default to a verbal greeting and a nod.
watch_outs.do: Greet with words and a nod, and follow your host's lead before any physical contact.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not lean in for a cheek touch with someone of the opposite gender unless they clearly initiate it.

watch_outs.title: Soles pointing at people
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, foot position is a minor faux pas; just avoid propping feet on furniture in someone's home.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, showing the soles of your feet is rude; keep both feet flat or tucked beneath you.
watch_outs.do: Sit with both feet on the floor or tucked under you, especially in a majlis or family home.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not cross an ankle over your knee so your sole points at anyone.

watch_outs.title: Public affection and dress
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, brief hand-holding is fine and public affection is kept modest, especially around elders.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, public kissing or hugging carries legal risk, and modest dress is expected in malls, government offices, and traditional areas.
watch_outs.do: Save affection for private settings and wear loose clothing covering shoulders and knees in public places.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not assume tourist zones exempt you from the law, and do not wear very short shorts, low-cut tops, or sheer fabrics in streets or lobbies.

watch_outs.title: Thumbs-up and OK sign
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, thumbs-up and the OK sign are friendly, positive gestures used freely.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, both are risky with older Emiratis and in business settings; a verbal thank-you or nod is safer.
watch_outs.do: Say 'shukran' or give a simple nod of approval instead.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not flash a thumbs-up or OK sign to a senior Emirati colleague or client.

watch_outs.title: Beckoning and pointing
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, a palm-down finger wave is already the polite way to call someone over, and pointing at people is avoided.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, a curled index finger is seen as a gesture for animals, and pointing at people should be done with the whole hand.
watch_outs.do: Call people with a palm-down wave and indicate with your whole open hand.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not curl one finger upward to beckon or jab your index finger at a person.

watch_outs.title: Refusing host's food
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, you hesitate then accept a small token portion or ask to take some home rather than refuse outright.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, refusing food offered by a host is rude; accept at least a small portion or a sip before declining more.
watch_outs.do: Take a little of whatever is offered, plus a sip of gahwa or tea, before politely saying you are full.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not wave away the tray or say no before tasting anything.

watch_outs.title: Eye contact across genders
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, friendly eye contact is normal, though juniors may glance down as a sign of respect.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, hold steady eye contact with your own gender but keep it brief and polite with the opposite gender in business.
watch_outs.do: Meet your counterpart's eyes briefly and warmly, then let your gaze rest naturally.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not hold a long, unbroken stare with an opposite-gender colleague or client.

watch_outs.title: Shoes at the door
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, you look for a pile of shoes or ask your host before taking shoes off.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, removing shoes is expected in most homes; watch your host and other guests at the entrance.
watch_outs.do: Check for a shoe rack or pile at the door and remove your shoes when you see one.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not walk past the entrance into a carpeted sitting room with your shoes still on.

watch_outs.title: Tipping and service charge
watch_outs.from_norm: In the Philippines, you check for a service charge line, then leave about 10% in cash with the server.
watch_outs.to_norm: In the UAE, tipping is appreciated but not obligatory; check the bill for a service charge, then leave about 10-15% in cash directly to staff.
watch_outs.do: Read the bill first, then hand cash to your server if you want it to reach them.
watch_outs.avoid: Do not add a tip on the card and assume the staff will receive it.
